meta.title: Microsoft Fluent 2 (Fluent UI v9) design tokens
meta.source: Programmatically extracted from installed @fluentui/react-theme webLightTheme/webDarkTheme/teamsHighContrastTheme, @fluentui/tokens typographyStyles, and brandColors.js brand ramps.
notes: Every token name X is exposed as a CSS custom property named --X by FluentProvider. Read it in CSS with var(--X) or in JS via the tokens object from @fluentui/react-components (tokens.X === "var(--X)").
semanticLight/semanticDark/semanticHighContrast contain the concrete resolved values for the built-in web themes.
brandRamp is the default web brand ramp (brandWeb). createLightTheme(brandVariants)/createDarkTheme(brandVariants) accept a BrandVariants object of 16 slots (10..160).
Typography ramp values are resolved to concrete px/weight from the light theme; they are identical in dark theme.

additionalSources.adds: color.aliasReference — alias to global token slot mapping, interaction state, and the 14 published categories.
additionalSources.licensing: Structured facts only (token names, global slot names, category and state labels). No descriptive prose reproduced.

additionalSources.adds: Same mapping in plain-table form; used only for the 13 aliases /color-tokens/ omits.

aliasReferenceMeta.title: Web alias colour tokens — alias token to global token slot map
aliasReferenceMeta.what: For every documented alias colour token: which global token slot (family[slot]) it resolves to in the light and dark web themes, plus the interaction state and the category the site files it under. Concrete hex values stay in semanticLight/semanticDark/semanticHighContrast.
aliasReferenceMeta.globalSlotSyntax: family[slot] — e.g. grey[16], brand[80], cranberry[tint60], whiteAlpha[50]. Literal values (white, black, transparent, rgba(...)) appear as-is.

verification.method: Every alias on /color-tokens/ carries a rendered swatch; its hex was compared with the value already in this file (extracted from the installed @fluentui/react-theme + @fluentui/tokens packages).
verification.conflictPolicy: The npm package is authoritative. Where the published page disagrees the package value is kept and the difference is recorded in "discrepancies" — scraped values never overwrite package values.

coverage.note: Tokens in "undocumentedOnSite" ship in the package and resolve normally; the published colour-token pages simply do not list them.

notes: The published pages document light and dark only — there is no high-contrast column. semanticHighContrast still comes from @fluentui/react-theme teamsHighContrastTheme.

/color-tokens2/ renders the same alias-to-global mapping as a plain table (no swatches, no headings, same <title>). It is a duplicate, not a second source: only the 13 aliases missing from /color-tokens/ were taken from it.
Shadow rows on /color-tokens2/ are truncated at the first comma of their rgba() value (published rendering defect), so shadow slots come from /color-tokens/ only.
Alias state rows map to the token name suffix: Rest = base name, Hover/Pressed/Selected/Disabled = the matching suffixed token.
